source_text: Omnes quoque Prophetas et Apostolos vel sanctos et evangelicos et antiquos, quibus Deus testimonium perhibet, non in comparatione sceleratorum, sed regula virtutum iustos fuisse. In futuro autem tempore mercedem esse factorum bonorum atque malorum, nec tamen ibi iuberi quemquam quae hic contempserit implere mandata
pass_a_gloss: All Prophets and Apostles also, or saints both of the Gospel and of old, to whom God bears testimony, were just not by comparison with criminals but by the rule of virtues. In the time to come there is a wage of good deeds and of bad, and yet no one is commanded there to fulfill the commandments he despised here.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: All the prophets, apostles, and saints, both those of the Gospel and those of ancient times, to whom God bears witness, were righteous by the standard of virtue, not by comparison with criminals.
In the time to come there is recompense for good deeds and for bad ones, and no one is commanded to fulfill there the commandments that they disregarded here.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
